<!-- pr-reviewer: ef77d89facd2a5cb1ceedbf3052734ee333c7681 -->
**Verdict: Ready for the maintainer to merge**

Thanks for the fix and for the clear write-up.

**What looks good**
- Test-only change (6 lines, `crates/ui/tests/gpu_render.rs`); no production code, dependencies, build scripts or workflows touched.
- The guard is taken at the top of `render_mode`, before `device_and_queue()`, and declared first, so it drops last. Device, queue and view are torn down while the lock is still held, which is the lifecycle the PR describes. Every test reaches the GPU through `render`/`render_mode`, so all nine are covered.
- A poisoned lock is recovered with `PoisonError::into_inner`, so one failing test does not cascade into the others. No `unwrap`/`expect` added.
- The comment states why the lock exists.

**Local results (merged with current main, Windows)**
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --test gpu_render` (CWD `crates/ui`) | 9 passed, 0 failed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --test gpu_render -- -D warnings` | clean |

Only the touched suite was run. I cannot reproduce the software-Vulkan SIGSEGV on this machine, so the fix is confirmed to be harmless here, not shown to cure the crash. That rests on your Fedora run.

**Requested before merge**
None.

**Notes (not blocking)**
- The body has a `Changelog:` line but no `Fixes #N`. If there is no tracking issue for this, that is fine for a test-only fix. If there is one, please link it.
- `crates/ui/tests/trace_composite.rs` and `trace_parity.rs` also have their own `device_and_queue()`. They are separate test binaries (separate processes), so this lock does not cover them. If they ever show the same crash, the same pattern applies.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
